releases.summary: Reliability fixes, and the .deb becomes the only Linux package.
changes: Discovery no longer stops for good after a single failed broadcast — a refused cycle costs one announcement instead of every future one.
Android discovery survives the server going away and coming back, instead of sticking on "No server found yet".
The client lock is released once rather than twice when the virtual display fails, so a reconnect is no longer answered as busy.
The .deb declares python3-dbus, without which the app failed at startup on a machine that did not already have it.
The .deb installs its files as root rather than under the build machine's user account.
The Snap package is no longer offered: strict confinement cannot create the virtual display at all, because Mutter's ScreenCast API is private and no snapd interface grants it.

releases.summary: Packaging fixes so the snap ships the H.264 plugins it needs and launches from the right directory.
changes: Snap bundles the two GStreamer plugins H.264 actually requires.
The launcher runs from the library directory, so the working directory can no longer shadow the install.

releases.summary: Touch input: the tablet can drive the pointer, plus hardware H.264 and a rebuilt site.
changes: Tap, drag, right-click and scroll on the tablet move the pointer on the PC.
Touch is off by default and negotiated per connection; old clients are unaffected.
The server serves only peers on a USB-attached interface, detected at runtime.
Hardware H.264 encoding with runtime encoder probing.

releases.summary: First public release — a real second display over USB, streamed as JPEG.
changes: GNOME ScreenCast capture of a dedicated virtual monitor.
Automatic server discovery over the USB tether.
